claim_being_audited: That model-card certification may proceed because aggregate performance clears threshold, provided the small-business support slice weakness is explicitly disclosed and no clean-certification claim is made absent an approved mitigation.
specific_concerns: Only the actor's summary is available; the underlying contents of the cited evidence are not admissible to this role as presented.
The packet relies on numerical threshold claims and slice-performance deltas that cannot be independently verified from the available record.

The conclusion depends on the unresolved predicate that the small-business support slice weakness is in fact materially disclosed in the certification packet, but the actual disclosure text is not provided.

The actor frames the result as certification-supportive, but the support level is only moderate and the evidence chain for materiality, thresholds, and mitigation status is incomplete from this vantage point.
unsupported_claims: The model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by 2.2 percentage points.
The small-business support slice is 1.1 points below its warning threshold and 2.6 points below its preferred threshold.
No approved mitigation currently removes exposure.
The smaller sample and wider confidence interval justify confirmation in the next evaluation batch.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BMCARD-004-A through BMCARD-004-E, not just the IDs.
Provide the actual model-card certification text showing the disclosed small-business support slice weakness.
Provide the governing threshold table or policy mapping used to substantiate the aggregate, warning, and preferred threshold comparisons.
Provide the record showing whether any mitigation was proposed, reviewed, approved, or rejected, including its current status.
Provide the evaluation results and sample-size/confidence-interval documentation for the small-business support slice.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates may support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty may reduce confidence but does not convert an unresolved materiality question into a clean certification.
Numeric performance claims, mitigation status, and disclosure sufficiency must be supported by admissible evidence, not actor characterization alone.
